events.title: Marie Antoinette is born in Vienna
events.description: Archduchess Maria Antonia of Austria was born into the Habsburg imperial family. At 14 she married the future Louis XVI of France, and she became queen consort in 1774.
events.significance: Her life, from the glittering court of Versailles to the guillotine in 1793, became a lasting symbol of the excesses of the old order and of the French Revolution.

events.title: North and South Dakota join the Union
events.description: President Benjamin Harrison signed the proclamations admitting North Dakota and South Dakota as the 39th and 40th states. The two were admitted together, and the order of their admission was deliberately left unrecorded.
events.significance: The double admission rounded out the northern Great Plains as states and marked a key step in the westward expansion of the United States.

events.title: The Balfour Declaration is issued
events.description: British Foreign Secretary Arthur James Balfour wrote to Lord Walter Rothschild. The letter expressed the government's support for a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine.
events.significance: The letter shaped British policy in the Middle East and remains central to debates over the region's history to this day.

events.title: The Spruce Goose takes flight
events.description: Howard Hughes piloted his giant wooden flying boat, the H-4 Hercules, on its only flight. It lifted off the water off Long Beach, California, and flew for about a mile.
events.significance: The largest aircraft of its day showed both the ambition and the limits of aviation engineering, and it became an enduring symbol of Hughes's daring.

events.title: The first crew arrives at the International Space Station
events.description: The first long-term residents, Expedition 1, docked with the station and moved in. The crew was American commander Bill Shepherd with Russian cosmonauts Yuri Gidzenko and Sergei Krikalev.
events.significance: Humans have lived continuously in orbit since this arrival, which began an era of international cooperation in space.
